Visvod became Gornebes's first permanent colony beyond Stenput in 783 A.E., following qualified scientific discovery in 749 and official registration as Dzelo-2 in 750.

Its established exploration route was conventional interstellar travel from Stenput, rather than one of the natural-jumphole passages used elsewhere in the region. Permanent settlement extended the inhabited territory of Gornebes beyond its founding capital, adding another community to the regional programme.

Dzelo-3 entered Gornebes's official survey register in 822 A.E., following qualified scientific discovery two years earlier. A natural jumphole connected the destination with Stenput, extending the region's exploration along a branch distinct from the conventional route toward Dzelo-2.

Official registration established the system's place within the Dzelo programme, but no permanent colony had yet been founded. The destination remained known by its survey designation.

Gureprist’s permanent settlement follows more than a century under the survey designation Dzelo-3. The system belongs to the natural exploration branch from Stenput, but its colonial foundation came after the later-registered Basanberg. Its history reflects the separate pace of discovery and settlement within Gornebes’s expanding regional programme.

Dzelo-4 entered Gornebes’s survey register as its exploration programme reached beyond the earliest regional colonies. Scientific discovery and official recognition have identified the destination before a permanent community gives it a proper name.

Basanberg became a permanent Gornebes colony in 926 A.E., following qualified scientific discovery in 884 and official registration as Dzelo-4 in 886. The settlement extended the inhabited frontier of a region whose scientific exploration had already reached several destinations beyond Stenput.

At the time Basanberg was established, the earlier-registered Dzelo-3 still lacked a permanent colony. The two systems illustrate how survey registration and permanent settlement advanced on different schedules within Gornebes's colonial programme.

Dzelo-5 entered Gornebes's official survey register in 959 A.E., following qualified scientific discovery two years earlier. A natural jumphole connected the destination with Gureprist, extending the explored branch outward from Stenput.

The new registration added another recognized system to Gornebes's regional programme, but permanent settlement had not yet been established. Dzelo-5 remained its official designation.

Obalput became a permanent Gornebes colony in 997 A.E., following its earlier discovery and registration as Dzelo-5. A natural jumphole connected the system with Gureprist, placing its settlement along the explored branch extending outward from Stenput.

The colony was founded during a period when older Cantums had begun obtaining sovereignty from the Continuance. That political fragmentation formed part of the historical circumstances of Obalput's establishment, while its own foundation belonged to Gornebes's continuing regional programme. The system retained its original Dzelo-5 identity through the subsequent changes in the sector's political order.

Dzelo-6 entered Gornebes's official survey register in 1018 A.E., following qualified scientific discovery in 1016. A natural passage connected the destination with Obalput, continuing the region's explored frontier beyond the earlier Dzelo colonies.

Registration established another recognized system within Gornebes, but no permanent colony or proper settlement name had yet been established. The destination remained officially designated Dzelo-6.

Plavput’s permanent colony continues the Dzelo programme beyond Gornebes’s earlier foundations. Its original Dzelo-6 identity records the surveying that preceded settlement, while its natural connection with Obalput belongs to the region’s outward exploration geography. The community carries that frontier from scientific recognition into a named colonial history.

Plavput began as Dzelo-6 in Gornebes’s outward programme and became a permanent colony on the natural branch beyond Obalput. Its original Gornebes foundation predates the sovereign order created by the Continuance’s dissolution. The postwar settlement of 1175 has made Plavput the sole official neutral border system for Zaklun and Gornebes. It is unaffiliated with both Cantums and outside their direct administration, placing an old regional colony within the new framework of regulated relations between independent states.

Dzelo-7 is a scientifically recognized destination in Gornebes’s original survey programme. Official registration followed its discovery, but its recorded history contains no permanent colonial foundation or proper settlement name. The system retains its place in the Dzelo sequence as an explored destination distinct from the region’s named colonies.

Dzelo-8 entered Gornebes's official survey register in 1130 A.E., following qualified scientific discovery two years earlier. A natural jumphole connected the destination with Obalput, placing it on another branch of the region's established exploration network.

The system received official recognition while Gornebes still belonged to the unified Continuance. Registration did not itself establish a permanent colony, and the destination remained known by its numerical designation.

Dulinpol’s permanent foundation carries an older Gornebes survey undertaking into the Cantum’s sovereign era. First registered as Dzelo-8 while Gornebes still belonged to the Continuance, the system now receives its proper name after peaceful independence. Its natural connection with Obalput belongs to the inherited geography of regional exploration, which has continued across the political separation.

Zhivete-1 entered the Continuance's official survey register in 639 A.E., following remote scientific qualification two years earlier. It was designated as the intended capital system of Vodravan, one of three distant Cantums planned for establishment through sleeper expeditions.

Registration established the destination's official identity, but did not signify a permanent colony or an active regional government. The expedition's conventional journey, the establishment of an inhabited community and the construction of an artificial receiving connection were separate stages of the founding programme.

The Zhivete sleeper expedition reached its destination in 705 A.E., following a conventional voyage begun in 647. Its settlers began constructing the infrastructure needed to sustain a permanent community among freshwater environments and fertile basins. In 715, the settlement received the name Vudegrad, replacing its original Zhivete-1 survey designation.

The colony had achieved permanent habitation, but its artificial receiving connection with Bujnasel was not yet operational. The expedition's designated leadership continued the founding undertaking without constituting the formally activated government of a subordinate Cantum.

In 725 A.E., Vudegrad's artificial receiving gate established an operational connection with Bujnasel in Drevnasel. The same milestone activated the central government's prior authorization for Vodravan, making Vudegrad the capital of the fifth Cantum of the Continuance.

The Zhivete expedition had reached the system in 705 and established a permanent colony in 715. With regular transport from the older systems now possible, the young Cantum could continue developing its agricultural, freshwater and supporting infrastructure while remaining under Drevnasel's central authority. Vodravan was the first of the three distant regions to complete the founding sequence.

Vudegrad’s history began with the Zhivete sleeper expedition and the work of building a community before reconnection to the Continuance. The successful link with Bujnasel established Vodravan’s formal government here, after which the region extended its settlement and survey programmes while developing agriculture, freshwater infrastructure and productive capabilities. Peaceful independence in 1153 has made Vudegrad the capital of a sovereign Cantum, with diplomacy and commerce continuing across the former internal political boundary.

Zhivete-2 has joined Vodravan’s register as its first outward destination beyond the capital. Scientific discovery and official recognition continue the programme established at Vudegrad, opening another colonial candidate before permanent settlement and proper naming.

Visdom became Vodravan's first permanent colony beyond Vudegrad in 768 A.E. The destination had qualified for scientific discovery in 738 and entered the official register as Zhivete-2 in 739.

A natural jumphole connected the system with Vudegrad, allowing the regional programme to extend its exploration beyond the capital. Visdom's foundation established a second permanently inhabited community within the growing Cantum, carrying its original survey identity into an expanding colonial territory.

Zhivete-3 has received official recognition as Vodravan’s outward programme advances beyond its earliest colonies. Its survey registration follows scientific discovery and records another destination before a permanent community supplies a proper settlement name.

Tolaput became a permanent Vodravan colony in 810 A.E., following qualified scientific discovery in 777 and official registration as Zhivete-3 in 779. A natural jumphole connected the destination with Visdom, the earlier colony reached from Vudegrad.

The settlement extended the inhabited frontier farther along the region's natural network. Tolaput became another established community in Vodravan's outward programme, retaining the history of Zhivete-3 as its original survey identity.

Zhivete-4 is an officially recognized destination in Vodravan’s continuing exploration programme. Registration follows its scientific discovery, extending the recorded frontier beyond the region’s earlier colonies without itself establishing permanent settlement.

Pulysten’s permanent settlement extends the natural branch explored beyond Tolaput. Its original Zhivete-4 designation records the scientific recognition that preceded the named colony. The community continues the sequence of foundations through which Vodravan developed an inhabited territory beyond Vudegrad and its earliest outward settlements.

Zhivete-5 entered Vodravan's official survey register in 917 A.E., following qualified scientific discovery two years earlier. A natural jumphole connected the destination with Tolaput, extending the growing regional programme along another branch beyond its original capital.

Official registration established the system's place within Vodravan's survey sequence, but no permanent colony or proper settlement name had yet been established. The destination remained known as Zhivete-5.

Drvhrid’s permanent community grew from the system registered as Zhivete-5. Its natural connection with Tolaput belongs to Vodravan’s outward exploration geography, while the founding of a colony has given the destination its proper name. The system’s origins lie within that regional programme, independent of any later international role.

Drvhrid was founded through Vodravan’s outward programme, with Zhivete-5 registration preceding its permanent settlement. The natural branch from Tolaput belongs to its early exploration geography. After Vodravan and Gornebes gained sovereignty, their inherited connections became part of relations between separate states. The settlement of 1175 has made Drvhrid their official neutral border system, unaffiliated with either Cantum and outside direct Cantum administration. Its original Vodravan history remains distinct from this new international role.

Zhivete-6 has received official registration during Vodravan’s continuing survey programme. Its recognition extends the regional sequence beyond the earlier frontier destinations, recording scientific discovery before permanent settlement and a proper colonial name.

Ravnvod became Vodravan's sixth permanently settled original Zhivete system in 1048 A.E., following qualified scientific discovery in 1003 and official registration as Zhivete-6 in 1005.

A natural jumphole connected the destination with Pulysten, extending the inhabited frontier along one of the branches beyond Tolaput. Its foundation continued Vodravan's colonial development while the Cantum remained a constituent region of the Continuance, preserving Zhivete-6 as its original survey identity.

Zhivete-7 entered Vodravan’s survey register as exploration continued beyond its named colonies. Scientific discovery and official recognition established the system’s place in the regional sequence. It retains that designation without a recorded permanent colonial foundation or proper settlement name.

Zhivete-8 was registered after Vodravan’s peaceful independence, continuing the survey programme begun during its time within the Continuance. Its official identity follows scientific discovery under the sovereign Cantum and records a destination without a permanent colony name. Political separation has preserved the original regional sequence.

Zhivete-9 extends Vodravan’s official survey sequence in the era after the Final Inter-Cantum War. Discovery and registration continue a scientific programme inherited from the unified Continuance and maintained under Vodravan’s sovereign government. The system is recorded under its survey designation without a permanent colonial foundation.
